hypothesis: If the claim holds, no amphibian (frog, toad, newt) is native to any truly oceanic island, while amphibians introduced by people do establish breeding populations on many of those same islands.
pass_criterion: Take a pre-registered list of 15 oceanic islands or archipelagos that have never been joined to a continent: Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Madeira, Cape Verde, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Bermuda, Mauritius, Réunion, Rodrigues, Society Islands, Marquesas and Easter Island. Query GBIF occurrences with classKey=131 (Amphibia), basisOfRecord in {PRESERVED_SPECIMEN, HUMAN_OBSERVATION, MATERIAL_SAMPLE}, and coordinates or island/country fields within these islands. After removing records flagged establishmentMeans=INTRODUCED/INVASIVE/MANAGED and species listed as introduced in the literature, 0 of the 15 islands should have a species with establishmentMeans=NATIVE. Remaining unflagged species must resolve to introductions on checking against AmphibiaWeb or IUCN native ranges, with at most 1 unresolved species. Also, at least 8 of the 15 islands must have at least one introduced amphibian species with at least 3 occurrence records (the 'introduced frogs thrive' clause).
fail_criterion: At least 1 of the 15 islands has an amphibian species with a verified native range that includes it (GBIF establishmentMeans=NATIVE, confirmed by IUCN or AmphibiaWeb). Also fails if fewer than 4 of the 15 islands have any established introduced amphibian, which would undercut the 'introduced frogs thrive' clause.
interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands' means islands far from continents that are of volcanic or coral origin and have never been land-connected. Modern geology gives a defensible list, and continental fragments are excluded, for example Seychelles, New Zealand, Madagascar, New Caledonia and the Caribbean's larger islands. 'Batrachians' maps to the class Amphibia. Caecilians are included in the test, as a conservative extension, since Darwin did not name them. 'Naturally absent' means no native populations. 'Introduced frogs thrive' means introduced populations are recorded as established or repeatedly observed. The sea-water mechanism (intolerance of salt water by adults and spawn) is not testable with occurrence data, so this plan tests only the distributional generalization and the thriving-when-introduced premise. Modern taxonomy and GBIF's backbone replace Darwin's names.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (Amphibia, class key 131), searched via the GBIF occurrence search and API
dataset.why_it_fits: The GBIF occurrence API (https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search) returns georeferenced amphibian records with the fields taxonKey, scientificName, establishmentMeans, island, islandGroup, countryCode, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude and basisOfRecord. These allow filtering by island and separating native from introduced records. Species lists per island can then be checked against AmphibiaWeb (https://amphibiaweb.org) and the IUCN Red List (https://www.iucnredlist.org) for native ranges.
